summary: Iter 48 orphan-memberships lens tested end-to-end. Backend: 8/9 pytest cases pass (shape+3 auth gates + duplicates seed/detect/purge + role-drift seed/detect/fix + dangling_archived via archive endpoint). 1 test failure exposes an algorithmic bug in multi_firm_staff detection. Frontend: /admin renders <OrphanMembershipsCard/> with header 'Data health · orphan memberships', badge '4 findings', Refresh button, and 5 collapsible rows each with the documented data-testid. Row expansion renders a table. Pro user is denied /admin (redirected to /pro/clients) — orphan-card not visible. Seeded a duplicate + client-role drift via Mongo, confirmed 'Purge duplicates' and 'Elevate to pro' buttons appear, click emits correct toast ('kept=32, deleted=2' and 'elevated=1'), and card refreshes with counts back to 0.

critical.issue: multi_firm_staff detection is algorithmically dead code — the union-find bridges companies via any pro they share, including the very user we're trying to flag. As soon as a candidate has pro memberships on companies A and B, that user themselves unions(A, B), so len(firms_per_user[uid]) collapses to 1 and they are never reported. Seeded test proves this: created 2 disjoint firms (pro_a on co_a, pro_b on co_b, no other shared pros) + a victim with pro memberships on BOTH — victim did NOT appear in multi_firm_staff. Fix should exclude the candidate user's own memberships when computing the firm partition, e.g. per-candidate union-find using only OTHER users' pro memberships, or partition by enterprise_id where available.

issues: React hydration warning in console: '<button> cannot be a descendant of <button>' from Layout.jsx line 336 — pre-existing, unrelated to iter48, but worth flagging.

action_items: Fix multi_firm_staff union-find in /app/backend/routes/admin.py so candidate users don't self-merge the firm partitions they span (exclude candidate's own pro memberships when building the union, or partition by enterprise_id).

rca of the issue: In /app/backend/routes/admin.py::orphan_memberships (lines 809-834), the algorithm builds firm partitions by unioning any two companies that share at least one pro user. However, the loop `for cids in pro_to_companies.values(): _union(cids[0], other)` iterates over ALL users, including the candidate later being checked for multi-firm status. Consequently, whenever a candidate holds pro memberships on companies belonging to two would-be-distinct firms, THE CANDIDATE THEMSELVES supplies the bridging edge that unions those firms into one, so firms_per_user[candidate]={single root} and len<2 fails the flagging condition. Reproduction: seed 3 users (pro_a exclusive to co_a, pro_b exclusive to co_b, victim on both). Expected: victim in multi_firm_staff with firm_count=2. Actual: multi_firm_staff==[]. Mitigation: for each candidate uid, rebuild the union-find using only pros OTHER than uid before computing that candidate's firms_per_user, or switch to a partition source that is independent of the memberships being audited (e.g. companies.enterprise_id).
